_comment: The border-design corpus for the BYOK border capability (tracks byok_svg_borders_20260927 archived + byok_border_prompt_adoption_20261006).
Each entry is a USER INSTRUCTION, in the shape a person would actually type into the BYOK box.
`scripts/border_design_generator.js` pairs it with the PRODUCT's own system message
(`AiLayout.buildMessages`, capabilities {arrange:false, border:true}) and sends the pair to the
live NOUS leg, so what is under test is the product prompt PLUS this instruction - polishing the
one and not the other would polish a prompt the extension never sends.
2026-10-06 (track byok_border_prompt_adoption_20261006, operator instruction "regenerate and
refreeze to adopt the 10/10 prompts"): the 11 instructions below are the 10/10 prompt texts from
the archived track's muse-loop on PROMPT QUALITY (temp/scratch/border_prompts_final.json, 5 rounds,
Muse primary + DeepSeek fallback, cumulative history + dispositions per round; every id reached
finalScore 10). They are adopted VERBATIM - title and criterion are unchanged, and the per-design
criteria remain exactly as the archived track's operator rulings left them (D-C/R-3/R-6/R-7
overrides). 05-celestial-arcs is ABSENT: it was retired from the canonical corpus by operator
ruling D3 (executed 2026-10-05; it left `designs` in the frozen fixture after its one permitted
regeneration failed the binding metric), and the 10/10 loop - which ran over the canonical set -
never scored a text for it. Keeping it here would invite a regeneration D3 precluded; its blobs
survive in the fixture variants.
`criterion` is the visual gate's per-design line. It is written to be DECIDABLE IN PIXELS: a
reviewer that cannot see it in the frame must answer NOT MET, so a criterion that names a
feeling rather than a drawn thing is a defect in this file.
`id` is stable and is what the collage label and the verdict file key on.

designs.title: Gilded double frame
designs.instruction: Draw a restrained double rule frame — TWO concentric rectangular rules, one inside the other, each ONE CONTINUOUS SOLID line unbroken around all four edges (no stroke-dasharray, no dash pattern, no tick marks, no mid-edge or corner breaks). Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 256 288" (match it exactly): stroke the outer rectangle inset 4 units from the viewBox edge and the inner rectangle 10 units further in, each with stroke-width 1.6 units, so both rules live entirely inside the border edge slices with the interior empty. Place one solid filled diamond (a square rotated 45 degrees, no stroke, diagonal 6 units) centred on each corner where the two rules cross, one per corner slice. Design for greyscale print: draw rules and diamonds in solid opaque black or near-black (#000 or #111) — the print pipeline renders the band in greyscale, so hue is not judged; do not spend ink trying to keep a colour. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 256 288\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 256 288" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and gradients: no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: Two concentric rectangular rules in a gold tone are both drawn as continuous SOLID lines closed around the full rectangle — no gaps or dashes anywhere on either rule — a diamond mark sits at each of the four corners, and no rule crosses the interior.

designs.title: Runic tick band
designs.instruction: Draw a band of angular rune ticks along the top and bottom edges with a plain rule on the left and right. Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 224 144" (match it exactly). Top and bottom: inside the top and bottom edge bands (strictly the outer 12% of the viewBox height) place at least 8 angular rune glyphs per band — each glyph 6-10 units tall and 4-7 units wide, built from 2-3 straight strokes with stroke-width 1.5 units — evenly spaced with a clear gap of at least one glyph-width between neighbours, none touching, none overlapping, every glyph fully inside the band. Left and right: inside the left and right edge bands (strictly the outer 8% of the viewBox width) draw one continuous vertical rule per side, stroke-width 2 units, running the full height of the slice. Keep the central 76% of the viewBox completely empty — only the edge bands and corner slices are painted; anything in the middle is cropped away by the border pipeline. Design for greyscale print: solid black or near-black strokes only, no hue, so the design survives the greyscale print filter. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 224 144\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 224 144" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and gradients: no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: A repeating sequence of at least six separate angular rune glyphs is visible along the top edge AND along the bottom edge, spaced evenly, with plain vertical rules on the left and right.

designs.title: Thorn vine
designs.instruction: Draw one continuous sinuous vine that frames all four edges, with small triangular thorns and oval leaves along its length. Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 224 256" (match it exactly): run the vine as a single unbroken stroke (stroke-width 3 units, round joins) that stays inside the outer edge bands (within 16 units of every edge) and passes through all four corner slices without lifting, so the border pipeline's edge and corner slices all receive ink — keep the central area empty, artwork in the middle of the viewBox is cropped away. On each edge place 6-9 solid triangular thorns pointing straight outward (perpendicular to that edge), each about 7 units wide at its base and 9 units tall, and 3-5 solid oval leaves each about 14 units long and 6 units wide, evenly spaced and attached to the vine. Because the border pipeline compresses the left and right rails horizontally (about 0.146 source units per device px horizontally against 0.923 vertically) draw the thorns and leaves on those two rails about 5 times wider in source than they should finally look, so the compression restores their proportions; express every size in viewBox units, never px. Design for greyscale print: use luminance contrast only — vine and thorns in solid near-black (#1A1A1A), leaves as light grey fills (#E8E8E8) with dark outlines — because the print pipeline renders the band in greyscale and hue is not judged. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 224 256\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 224 256" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and gradients: no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: A single continuous sinuous vine path is traceable along all four edges, with thorns or leaves projecting from it on at least three of the four edges.

designs.title: Dragon scale rail
designs.instruction: Draw a rail of overlapping dragon scales around the border, scutes pointing outward, the SAME source scale rail reused on all four edges. Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 800 800" (match it exactly): paint the scale rail as a continuous band that touches the outer edge of the viewBox on all four sides and fills the four corner slices — every edge band fully painted (at least 90% coverage per edge), no transparent gap wider than 6 units between neighbouring scales, each scale overlapping its neighbour with a visible tucked edge. Draw the scales horizontally elongated (about 3x wider than tall) with thick outlines and stroke-width at least 4 units so that after the border pipeline compresses the left and right rails the scales still read as normal overlapping scales rather than slivers — the four edges are judged aspect-independently, so do not try to make the rendered rails look pixel-identical to the top and bottom. Point each scale's tip straight outward from its own edge (top edge scales point up, bottom down, left left, right right) with a consistent overlap direction around the perimeter. Keep the middle of the viewBox empty. Design for greyscale print: solid high-contrast greyscale outlines only, no hue dependence. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 800 800\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 800 800" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and gradients: no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: Overlapping scale shapes are drawn in rows along the border, each scale visibly tucked under or over its neighbour, and the rows read as the same texture on the left/right as on the top/bottom.

designs.title: Chainmail interlace
designs.instruction: Draw an interlocking chainmail ring border: a four-in-one weave whose rings overlap in an alternating over-under interlock. Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 224 144" (match it exactly): fill the outer 24% bands — 53.76 units deep on the left and right, 34.56 units deep on the top and bottom, including the four 53.76x34.56 corner slices, which is exactly the depth the border pipeline slices — by distributing staggered rows of hollow rings across the FULL band depth, from the viewBox edge all the way to the inner band boundary, with the innermost row touching that boundary; the band is 34.56 units deep on the top and bottom and 53.76 on the sides, and the rings are 10-12 units across, so use as many rows as the depth requires (at least two per band) rather than a fixed pair. Each ring is unfilled (fill="none") with outer diameter 10-12 units, stroke-width 2 units, and neighbouring rings overlap by about one third of their diameter in an alternating over-under interlock, each row offset by half a ring from the one inside it. Continue the weave through all four corner slices so no corner is empty, and leave the central 116.48 x 74.88 area empty and transparent. Design for tall-section compression: the left and right bands are compressed horizontally about 6 times more than vertically, so keep stroke-width at 2 units or more and space the rings so they stay distinct after compression rather than merging into a grey smear. Design for greyscale print: black to dark-grey ring strokes (#000 to #444) on the transparent background only, no hue, with high luminance contrast so the weave survives the greyscale print filter. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 224 144\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 224 144" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and flat colour fills and strokes — no gradients, no patterns, no filters, no masks, and no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: At least eight separate ring shapes are visible around the border, drawn so consecutive rings visibly overlap and interlock rather than sitting apart as dots.

designs.title: Concentric corner arcs
designs.instruction: Draw three nested quarter-circle arcs in each of the four corners. Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 224 144" (match it exactly) and centre each corner's arcs exactly on that viewBox corner point — top-left (0,0), top-right (224,0), bottom-right (224,144), bottom-left (0,144) — with the arcs curving outward toward that corner point, identical nesting direction in all four corners. Use radii 10, 20 and 30 units: all three are smaller than the border pipeline's slice depth on BOTH axes (53.76 units horizontally, 34.56 units vertically), so every arc stays entirely inside its own 24% corner slice and never crosses into an edge slice. Keep ALL ink strictly inside the outer 24% of each axis (53.76 x 34.56 units) on all four sides and leave the middle 116 x 75 area completely empty with no paths, fills or strokes — the pipeline paints only the source's edge and corner slices, so anything in the middle of the viewBox is cropped away before any pixel exists. Give each corner group a short straight rule segment (stroke-width 3 units) running along each adjoining edge band so every edge slice carries ink as well as every corner slice. Draw the corner arcs as true quarter-circles — the corner slices are painted at their own size and are NOT stretched by the pipeline, so do not pre-distort them; only the straight edge rules run along a scaled axis, and a straight line cannot be deformed by that scaling. Strokes: fill="none", stroke="#0a0a0a", stroke-width="3", stroke-linecap="round", stroke-linejoin="round", stroke-opacity="1", written as presentation attributes directly on each element, with no dash pattern and no opacity below 1; keep every stroke a flat colour. Design for greyscale print: shape and nesting are judged, not hue. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 224 144\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 224 144" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and flat colour fills and strokes — no gradients, no patterns, no filters, no masks, and no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: In each of the four 56 device px corner boxes at grayscale, at least three separate concentric solid opaque unbroken dark quarter-circle arcs are countable as distinct strokes fully inside the corner, and straight solid dark rules connect the corner groups along each edge inside the 56 device px band.

designs.title: Flame crest rails
designs.instruction: Draw bold flame tongues along the left and right edges with a plain rule along the top and bottom. Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 224 256" (match it exactly): inside the left and right edge bands (strictly the outer 15% of the viewBox width) place 4-6 flame tongues per side, each a single solid filled shape (no stroke-only outlines) whose base spans at least 12% of the viewBox width (about 27 units) and whose body tapers to a sharp point aiming straight inward toward the centre of the page. Draw every flame at least 3 times wider than it is tall in source viewBox units, because the border pipeline compresses the left and right rails horizontally (about 0.146 source units per device px horizontally against 0.923 vertically on a tall section), so the horizontal exaggeration is what leaves visibly bold wide tongues instead of slivers — express every size in viewBox units, never device px. Inside the top and bottom edge bands draw one plain solid straight rule each (stroke-width 2.5 units, full width), and stop all flame shapes before the corner slices so corners form only from the meeting of the edge artwork. Keep the middle of the viewBox empty — artwork in the middle is cropped away. Design for greyscale print: solid near-black or mid-grey flame fill (#111 to #555) with strong luminance contrast against the background, no hue dependence, so the flames survive the greyscale print filter. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 224 256\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 224 256" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and gradients: no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: FILLED flame tongues, each at least 8px wide at its base and clearly tapering to a sharp point, are drawn along the left edge AND the right edge; the tongues point inward on both sides; and the top and bottom edges carry only a plain straight rule.

designs.title: Frost shard frame
designs.instruction: Draw sharp angular ice shards around all four edges, each shard faceted from at least two straight line segments. Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 224 256" (match it exactly): inside each edge band place 6-9 shards (each 10-16 units long, 5-8 units wide at its base, spaced 4-8 units apart, outlines never merging), and inside each of the four corner slices place a denser cluster of at least 5 shards radiating outward from the corner point — visibly busier than the straight edges. Draw the shards wider than tall in source coordinates so the border pipeline's horizontal compression on the left and right rails keeps them sharp and legible instead of collapsing them into slivers, and keep every shard strictly inside the edge bands and corner slices — the middle of the viewBox stays empty and is cropped away. Design for greyscale print: light grey to white shard fills (#FFFFFF to #E8E8E8) with dark grey to black outlines (#222222 to #000000, stroke-width 1.5-2 units), no blue or any hue, so the crystals survive the greyscale print filter with strong luminance contrast. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 224 256\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 224 256" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and gradients: no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: Sharp angular shard shapes are drawn along the edges, every shard is visibly faceted by at least two straight segments, and each of the four corners carries a denser multi-arm crystalline cluster than the edge run.

designs.title: Ink brush stroke
designs.instruction: Draw a calligraphic ink brush frame: one wet, uneven stroke running around the border with visible thick-to-thin variation. Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 224 144" (match it exactly): the brush stroke forms ONE continuous closed loop (no gaps, no dry-brush transparency holes, opacity 1 everywhere) centred about 6 units inside the viewBox edge with stroke width varying between 3 and 8 units — the variation runs ALONG the length of each edge (taper and pressure swells parallel to the edge direction), never across the stroke width, so the border pipeline's compression of the side rails keeps the modulation legible instead of smearing it into slivers. Carry the loop fully through all four corner slices with overlapping rounded joins so every corner carries solid ink, and add one small solid round ink dot (radius about 2 units) inside the top edge band, offset about 14 units from the top-left corner along the top edge. Keep the middle of the viewBox completely empty — artwork in the middle is cropped away. Design for greyscale print: solid opaque black ink only, no hue. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 224 144\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 224 144" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and gradients: no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: The border is drawn as a stroke whose thickness varies visibly along its length (not a constant-width rule), the stroke reads as continuous around the frame, and at least one small detached ink dot is visible near a corner.

designs.title: Starlit void band
designs.instruction: Draw a dark solid band around the border with small stars scattered inside the band and a thin light inner rule. Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 224 144" (match it exactly): build the band as four solid edge-anchored rectangles (outer 12 units of the viewBox on all four sides, joined through the four corner slices) so every edge band is fully painted (at least 90% coverage per edge) with no interior gap wider than 6 units; keep the central area empty. Inside the band — never in the centre, never crossing the inner rule — scatter 20-40 small filled stars or dots, each 1.5-2.5 units across, using compact round shapes that stay point-like after the border pipeline's compression of the side rails. Inset a thin continuous inner rule (stroke-width 1.5 units, no dash pattern) 3 units inside the band's inner edge. Design for greyscale print with luminance only: band fill near-black (#0A0E1A or #111827, luminance under 15%), inner rule and stars light grey (#C8C8D0, luminance over 75%) so the contrast survives the greyscale print filter — do not rely on hue such as blue or silver. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 224 144\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 224 144" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and gradients: no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: A dark filled band is drawn around the border, at least ten small star marks are scattered inside that dark band, and a thin lighter rule runs along the band's interior edge.

designs.title: Celtic knotwork rails
designs.instruction: Draw celtic knotwork bands along the top and bottom edges with a plain rule on the left and right. Anchor the artwork in a viewBox of "0 0 224 256" (match it exactly): inside the top and bottom edge bands (strictly the outer 16% of the viewBox height) weave 2-3 continuous strands per band, each strand stroke-width 2.2 units, with strand crossings spaced at least 12 units apart — at every crossing show the over-under weave as a real gap (a 1.5-unit break in the under-strand where the over-strand passes continuously over it), never by colour, shadow or stroke-weight change, so each strand can be followed over and under at a glance. Inside the left edge band (x = 0 to 36) and the right edge band (x = 188 to 224) draw one plain continuous rule per side (stroke-width 2.5 units, full height, no interweaving, no crossings). Let the rail strands run into the four corner slices and terminate as simple continuations — no corner medallions — so every corner slice carries ink. Keep the middle of the viewBox completely empty; artwork in the middle is cropped away. Design for greyscale print: solid near-black strands on the transparent background only, no hue. Reply with ONE JSON object only ({"border": {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 224 256\" ...>...</svg>"}, "note": "one short sentence"}) — no prose, no markdown fence, no moves/hide keys. The svg element MUST carry viewBox="0 0 224 256" and stay a complete static element under 16000 characters, drawn only with rect/path/circle/polygon/line/g and gradients: no script, no on* attributes, no foreignObject, no animation elements, no text, no image, no use, no href or xlink:href that does not start with "#", no @import, and no style element, class attribute or style attribute anywhere (write every presentation attribute inline on its element).
designs.criterion: On the top rail and on the bottom rail an interlaced strand pattern is visible, at least one crossing is drawn with an over/under break rather than a plain intersection, and the left and right edges carry a simpler treatment.
